newsitem.title: USA: Lehman uses most muni consultants - report.
newsitem.headline: Lehman uses most muni consultants - report.

text.p: Lehman Brothers is the municipal bond market's heaviest user of consultants, with 13 on its payroll, according to a report by Grant's Municipal Bond Observer.

The newsletter said in its May 30 issue that it surveyed filings made by the industry's top underwriters to the Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board. The MSRB requires firms to disclose the names and salaries of individuals they hire to help secure muni bond work.
Lehman hired 13 of the 113 named in the filings reviewed, followed closely by PaineWebber Group Inc at 12.
Underwriting firms generally employ consultants for their technical expertise on specific types of bonds, or because the firm does not have a local presence on the consultant's home turf.

But the use of consultants has come under fire by public interest groups. They charge that some consultants ignore conflicts of interest, cashing in on political connections or past jobs in government to steer bond deals to clients without regard to qualifications.
The MSRB instituted the disclosure requirement, known as Rule G-38, in response to the controversy.

According to the disclosure documents, J.P. Morgan Securities Inc, a unit of J.P. Morgan & Co, hired 10 consultants; Smith Barney Inc, a unit of Travelers Group Inc, listed nine, and Bear Stearns Cos Inc had eight.
Merrill Lynch & Co, one of the market's largest underwriters, told the MSRB it had not hired any consultants, according to Grant's.
Salaries for the consultants listed totalled at least $4.1 million, not including bonuses.

The highest paid consultant found by Grant's was Larry Mars, an official with Bio-Reclamation Technologies Inc. Miller & Schroeder said it pays Mars $300,000 a year to advise the firm on solid waste and other environmental issues in California.
